messages.subject: Random Effect Specifications
parts:
Hi All,

I have been trying to compare uncertainty estimates with various prior specifications of a simple varying intercept model (predicting Democratic vote). The baseline model (Bayes_0_100_uniform) is below.

data {
  int<lower=0> N;                                         // sample size
  int<lower=0> n_age;                                     // number of age categories
  int<lower=0> n_race;                                    // number of race categories
  int<lower=0> n_edu;                                     // number of education catoegories
  int<lower=0> n_party_id;                                // number of party-categories
  int<lower=0,upper=1> gender[N];                         // gender for each respondent
  int<lower=0,upper=n_age> age[N];                        // age for each respondent
  int<lower=0,upper=n_edu> edu[N];                        // edu for each respondent
  int<lower=0,upper=n_race> race[N];                      // race for each respondent
  int<lower=0,upper=n_party_id> party_id[N];              // party_id for each respondent
  real <lower=0,upper=1> vote_prev_state[N];              // 2012 statevote at the individual-level
  int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];                              // vote-choice
}
parameters {
  
  real beta;                                              // coefficient for female                    
  vector[n_age] a_age ;                                   // coefficient for age 
  vector[n_edu] a_edu;                                    // coefficient for edu 
  vector[n_race] a_race;                                  // coefficient for race 
  vector[n_party_id] a_party_id;                          // coefficient for party_id 
  real gamma;                                             // previous vote- slope
  real<lower=0> sigma_age;
  real<lower=0> sigma_edu;
  real<lower=0> sigma_race;
  real<lower=0> sigma_party;

}


model {                                                 // Prior specifications
sigma_age~uniform(0,100);
sigma_edu~uniform(0,100);
sigma_race~uniform(0,100);
sigma_party~uniform(0,100);


  gamma~normal(0,5);                                  // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%
  beta~normal(0,5);                                   // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%
  a_age~normal(0,sigma_age);                          // estimate sigma separately
  a_edu~normal(0,sigma_edu);                          // estimate sigma separately
  a_race~normal(0,sigma_race);                        // estimate sigma separately
  a_party_id~normal(0,sigma_party);                   // estimate sigma separately

for (i in 1:N) {                                        //Likelihood 
real y_hat;
    y_hat <- 
    beta*gender[i]
    +a_age[age[i]]
    +a_edu[edu[i]]
    +a_party_id[party_id[i]]
    +a_race[race[i]]+gamma*vote_prev_state[i];
    y[i] ~ bernoulli_logit(y_hat);
  } 
  }


From here, I change the prior specifications on the sigmas for the random effects to be truncated uniform on the 0-Infinity interval (Bayes_unbounded_uniform; the canned STAN prior if the variance-prior is not made explicit), and I remove the prior completely, bounding the random-effect coefficients such that 95% of their probability mass falls between -10 and 10, like so (Bayes_no_prior):

  gamma~normal(0,5);                                  // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%
  beta~normal(0,5);                                   // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%
  a_age~normal(0,5);                                  // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%
  a_edu~normal(0,5);                                  // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%
  a_race~normal(0,5);                                 // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%
  a_party_id~normal(0,5);                             // embed 95% of the probability mass between 0.1 and 99.9%



All three specifications produce very different credible intervals (the last one even different point-estimates), see CIs.pdf (attached; also includes uncertainty estimates from Glmer and Glmer2Stan). All credible intervals are actually wider than the one produced by Glmer. I especially fail to understand why the no-prior-specification yields results that are fundamentally different. Help is appreciated! Data and reproducible code is attached.

Many thanks,
Tobi
